description:
Start a backtest of one saved strategy over a window of history. Takes a strategy_id -- it reads the stored strategy's own rules, asset, timeframe and risk parameters. The recorded market is the default; pass quote_token and/or market_data_venue when the person chooses another quote or execution venue. An omitted choice keeps its recorded value. Check and report the selected market; never silently substitute a feed. IT RETURNS A SUBMISSION, NOT A RESULT: a real backtest takes minutes, so this hands back the run's id and the config it will use, and the metrics arrive on their own once the engine finishes. Tell the person it is running; do not call this again for the same question, and do not wait. It consumes a unit of the user's monthly backtest allowance at submission -- so it CHECKS THE STRATEGY FIRST, and a refusal costs nothing: a problem (verify_strategy's problems) always refuses, and a signal parameter still at its library default refuses until you either save chosen values or pass acknowledge_defaults=true to stand by the defaults deliberately. One (strategy, window) is ONE measurement: submitting the same strategy over the same dates again is refused and the existing run named -- read that with get_backtest instead. Both start_date and end_date are required: name the days, so the same question asked next week gives the same answer. Every message carries the current time, so work them out from that.

[Access: pay 0.10 USDC via x402 (PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header) OR authenticate with an API key. An x402-capable client will auto-pay; API-key clients pay nothing per call.]

acknowledge_defaults.description: Pass True to submit even though signal parameters are at their library defaults -- an explicit statement that the defaults were considered and stood by, never a way to skip considering them.

engine_generation.description: Only set when the person specifies an engine generation; omitted uses latest.

market_data_venue.description: Exact venue of the requested market.

quote_token.description: Quote currency of the requested market.

start_date.description: ISO start of the window, e.g. 2026-01-01.

name: run_backtest
